The second dumbest creature in the universe, this creature's thought patterns go swim, swim, hungry, swim, swim, hungry. They'll eat anything alive and moving near them, though they prefer heroes.  ”—Commander Keen 4 Manual
The Dopefish is a buck-toothed fish found in the Well of Wishes in Commander Keen: Goodbye Galaxy!. The Dopefish is the second dumbest creature in the universe; the first dumbest is mentioned in the Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy as the Ravenous Bugblatter Beast of Traal that believes if you can't see it, it can't see you, thus making you safe from it if you throw a towel over your head.
The Dopefish was originally drawn by Tom Hall as a stupid fish, but it became extremely popular with fans of Commander Keen. Apogee Software then started to use it for its tech support staff. It then became a gag among Id Software, Apogee, and their friends to put the Dopefish as a cameo character in their games.

Some assembly required.  Video assembly guide included (in AVI).
Note 1: This is my second experiment in posing a model before preparing it for STL printing.  In this case, I wasn't able to fit all the pieces on a 15 cm X 15 cm plane, so I have the six components in separate STL files in the same folder.  The video assembly guide and the pictures reflect this.

I can export non-animated models to that format, and I can export models to that format with the armature intact; but, while the models deform with the armature before the export, afterwards they don't.  If anyone has had success exporting to .X format in Blender with a model that deforms with the armature, and can give me specific instructions on how I can get it to work for me, please let me know.  I look forward to comments on this subject, as well as comments on the assembly guides and the models I've uploaded here.

description_text:
A simple ceramic coffee mug created with Blender 2.73 and rendered in Cycles. In this file are three mugs in three different colors included. Yellow, red and blue.
YOU WANT A LOW POLY GAME READY VERSION OF THIS MODEL? JUST LET ME KNOW!
|| GEOMETRY ||
Clean geometry, quads only. No ngons!
|| TEXTURES ||
This model uses only one noise texture as a bumpmap for a slight displacement. The texture is generated with Cycles nodes itself.

description_text:
Let me know if you print this file because I'd love to see it!
♦ 
Notes: 

  - 3D print ready model for Harley Quinn Black Mask cosplay

  - Files included are STL *, **OBJ * , **FBX

  - This is a fan-made item for Harley Quinn cosplayers

♦ 
Dimensions:
I designed the model to be: 15 x 5.45 x 9.91 cm
Feel free to rescale as desired
♦ 
DIY & Finishing:
After printing out your raw print, I recommend priming it with automotive car primer and sanding it. Repeat this as needed to get the desired to get the result. Have a look at Punished Props videos on YouTube for a better explanation with a demonstration ( link: https://youtu.be/pnqntteQx80 )Start with coarser grit sandpaper, and work your way down to finer grits. Sometimes I use wet-and-dry paper to get a really smooth (and sometimes shiny) finish. It really all depends on the result you want.
You can either use the 3d print itself, or make a silicone rubber mould and cast it in resin.
To get a metallic or chrome finish, I've seen Alclad II chrome airbrush paint recommended the most - and from what I've seen, it has the best results of all the method I've looked at so far. I've yet to try this for myself, but I suggest you look into this paint because I think you'll like the results.
Whatever method you use to decorate your 3d print, the finish might wear off. My dad likes to use varnish for boats because they're designed to be hard-wearing. I haven't tested this but I plan to look into it.

description_text: The national emblem or coat of arms of Indonesia is called Garuda Pancasila. The main part of the Indonesian national emblem is the Garuda with a heraldic shield on its chest and a scroll gripped by its legs. The shield's five emblems represent Pancasila, the five principles of Indonesia's national ideology. The Garuda claws gripping a white ribbon scroll inscribed with the national motto Bhinneka Tunggal Ika written in black text, which can be loosely translated as Unity in Diversity. Garuda Pancasila was designed by Sultan Hamid II from Pontianak, supervised by Sukarno, and was adopted as the national emblem on 11 February 1950.

description_text:
Game-ready starfish models and a geometry nodes setup for random distribution in any environment.
All varieties are grouped into a single blender file, including a geometry nodes setup for distributing the starfish over an object. Each variety is also included as a separate fbx file in highpoly and lowpoly versions, which are optimized for Unity and Unreal.
The detailed, high-res models are ideal for close-up rendering. The lowpoly versions are optimized for use as background props in larger scenes. The included Blender file contains a geometry nodes setup that distributes the starfish over any object, so you can quickly add them as ground clutter to your scenes.
Poly Counts:
High-poly versions contain between 1,510 and 26,501 vertices per model. Low poly versions have between 100 and 2,800 vertices per model. All models are UV unwrapped with non-overlapping islands.
Note: highpoly versions have clean topology and use quads (and n-gons to fill the center on their undersides). Lowpoly versions do not have clean topology, and use tris instead of quads.
Materials:
Each starfish has its own color map (2048 x 2048) and uses a procedural normal map. Color maps, materials, and preview renders are all labeled with the id number of the corresponding starfish.

Are You a Ninja Turtles  Fan?

Raphael, nicknamed Raph, is a fictional superhero and one of the four main characters of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles comics and all related media and second oldest/mid-middle-child of the turtle brothers
He is usually depicted wearing a red eye mask; in this regard he is the only turtle to retain the color in all media, whereas the others each received a different color. Raphael wields twin sai, the points of which are usually sharpened, as his primary weapon. Raphael is most famous for his temperamental personality, being short-tempered, aggressive, sullen, maddened, and rebellious.He is portrayed in most interaction as speaking with a Brooklyn accent. It may be a coincidence, but the fact that he has a bad and fiery attitude and temper and the fact that his mask is still red may be linked, since the color red is typically associated with anger.
The origin of Raphael's anger is not always fully explored, but in some incarnations appears to stem partly from the realization that they are the only creatures of their kind and ultimately alone. He also has a somewhat rival relationship with his only older brother Leonardo because he is seen as the group's leader. Raphael also gives his younger and youngest brother Michelangelo a hard time because of Michelangelo’s fiery optimism. He is the second eldest of the turtles, and second-in-command. Like all of the brothers, he is named after a Renaissance artist; in this case, he is named after the 16th-century Italian painter Raphael. In 2011, Raphael placed 23rd on IGN's Top 100 Comic Book Heroes, a list that did not feature any of his brothers. He is the only Teenage Turtle brother whose name does not end in the letter O
In the earliest black-and-white Mirage Comics, Raphael was the most violent turtle and had a tendency for going berserk either in battle or when his temper flared up. He has a somewhat cynical and sarcastic sense of humor. In later issues, it's shown that he is not particularly fond of the supernatural, stating so explicitly in Tales of Raphael: Bad Moon Rising.
Raphael mellowed somewhat as the series went on, possibly a key moment for his character development was when he allowed Leonardo to go in alone to defeat The Shredder after nearly being killed by the Foot Elite. Since then, he has been less likely to challenge Leonardo's leadership, and on the whole is more friendly towards his family and allies.
Of his three brothers, Raphael is actually closest to Michelangelo, having stated this in the fourth issue of the Mirage TMNT comics. Raphael often shows a caring, more laid-back, side of himself when around his youngest brother, frequently indulging the youngest turtle emotionally when at home and ferociously protecting him from harm when in battle. Raphael openly admits that the mere thought of his youngest brother being grievously injured causes him to experience violent rage. In his self-titled one-shot miniseries, Raphael meets human vigilante Casey Jones, his foil, who is more violent and unstable than he was. Despite their brutal first meeting, the two have since formed a close bond.
In the Mirage comic book series' Volume 4, he is still the most violent turtle, but is more sociable. After having been bitten by a vampire-like creature, he experienced a further mutation, and became a large, dinosaur-like version of himself. He went into a state of berserk animal rage because of it, but with some guidance by an inner manifestation of Master Splinter, he regained his original mentality and later assisted Leonardo and Casey Jones in tracking down the vampires who attacked him. This is also somewhat similar to an earlier storyline during Volume 1, where Raphael was attacked by a leech-like creature who, when sucking his blood, also drained him of the mutagen in his body and reverted him to a small turtle. The leech itself mutated and vanished, prompting the remaining turtles to follow it. Finally, after tracking down the creature, Raphael manages to bite it and pierce its skin, thereby drinking its blood and mutating back.
This incarnation of Raphael appeared in the crossover special Turtles Forever voiced by Sean Schemmel.

description_text:
6 unique, game-ready starfish models. All varieties are grouped into a single blender file, including a geometry nodes setup for distributing the starfish over an object. Each variety is also included as a separate fbx file in highpoly and lowpoly versions, which are optimized for Unity and Unreal.
The detailed, high-res models are ideal for close-up rendering, while the lowpoly versions are optimized for use as background props in larger scenes. The included Blender file contains a geometry nodes setup that distributes the starfish over any object, so you can quickly add them as ground clutter to your scenes.
Poly Counts:
High-poly versions contain between 1,510 and 26,501 vertices per model. Low poly versions have between 100 and 2,800 vertices per model. All models are UV unwrapped with non-overlapping islands.
Note: highpoly versions have clean topology and use quads (and n-gons to fill the center on their undersides). Lowpoly versions do not have clean topology, and use tris instead of quads.
Materials:
Each starfish has its own color map (2048 x 2048) and uses a procedural normal map. Color maps, materials, and preview renders are all labeled with the id number of the corresponding starfish.

description_text:
6 unique, game-ready starfish models. All varieties are grouped into a single blender file, including a geometry nodes setup for distributing the starfish over an object. Each variety is also included as a separate fbx file in highpoly and lowpoly versions, which are optimized for Unity and Unreal.
The detailed, high-res models are ideal for close-up rendering, while the lowpoly versions are optimized for use as background props in larger scenes. The included Blender file contains a geometry nodes setup that distributes the starfish over any object, so you can quickly add them as ground clutter to your scenes.
Poly Counts:
High-poly versions contain between 1,510 and 26,501 vertices per model. Low poly versions have between 100 and 2,800 vertices per model. All models are UV unwrapped with non-overlapping islands.
Note: highpoly versions have clean topology and use quads (and n-gons to fill the center on their undersides). Lowpoly versions do not have clean topology, and use tris instead of quads.
Materials:
Each starfish has its own color map (2048 x 2048) and uses a procedural normal map. Color maps, materials, and preview renders are all labeled with the id number of the corresponding starfish.

description_text:
Game-ready starfish models and a geometry nodes setup for random distribution in any environment.
All varieties are grouped into a single blender file, including a geometry nodes setup for distributing the starfish over an object. Each variety is also included as a separate fbx file in highpoly and lowpoly versions, which are optimized for Unity and Unreal.
The detailed, high-res models are ideal for close-up rendering. The lowpoly versions are optimized for use as background props in larger scenes. The included Blender file contains a geometry nodes setup that distributes the starfish over any object, so you can quickly add them as ground clutter to your scenes.
Poly Counts:
High-poly versions contain between 1,510 and 26,501 vertices per model. Low poly versions have between 100 and 2,800 vertices per model. All models are UV unwrapped with non-overlapping islands.
Note: highpoly versions have clean topology and use quads (and n-gons to fill the center on their undersides). Lowpoly versions do not have clean topology, and use tris instead of quads.
Materials:
Each starfish has its own color map (2048 x 2048) and uses a procedural normal map. Color maps, materials, and preview renders are all labeled with the id number of the corresponding starfish.

description_text:
A canoe is a lightweight narrow water vessel, typically pointed at both ends and open on top, propelled by one or more seated or kneeling paddlers facing the direction of travel and using a single-bladed paddle.[1]
In British English, the term canoe can also refer to a kayak,[2] while canoes are then called Canadian or open canoes to distinguish them from kayaks.
Canoes were developed by cultures all over the world, including some designed for use with sails or outriggers. Until the mid-1800s the canoe was an important means of transport for exploration and trade, and in some places is still used as such, sometimes with the addition of an outboard motor. Where the canoe played a key role in history, such as the northern United States, Canada, and New Zealand, it remains an important theme in popular culture.
Canoes are now widely used for competition and pleasure, such as racing, whitewater, touring and camping, freestyle and general recreation. Canoeing has been part of the Olympics since 1936. The intended use of the canoe dictates its hull shape, length, and construction material. Historically, canoes were dugouts or made of bark on a wood frame,[3] but construction materials evolved to canvas on a wood frame, then to aluminum. Most modern canoes are made of molded plastic or composites such as fiberglass.

description_text:
New realease v1.3
With this revision, the following improvements have been made:
1 - New hinge design, now it is more functional and easier to print.
2 - Improved the locking mechanism of the key, with a more functional design.
3 - Only four components to print and the hinge has been simplified with a more robust design.
With this project I'd like to present a very useful tool for carpfishing enthusiasts.Based on a revolutionary concept, this tool is used like a classic Bait Rocket but has many more advantages.The perfectly aerodynamic shape, which resembles a missile, makes it encounter minimal resistance in flight and thanks to its wings it maintains a very precise trajectory even in strong winds.The Spomb releases its contents instantly upon impact with water. It is a very effective feeder, to be used with SPOD carp fishing rods for baiting operations. The locking mechanism is very strong and does not open in the launch. The aerodynamic shape allows launches even up to 180 meters. The SPOMB can be used for baiting with pellets, boilies, hemp, corn, dog biscuits, bread, etc.
Features:

  - Streamlined design for minimal air resistance.

  - Enhances accuracy and efficiency in baiting swims.

  - Dimensions: 150mm length, 60mm diameter.

Instructions:
1) Download the design files for the 3D fully printable Rocket.
2) Use a 3D printer to print the Rocket in a single piece.
3) Once printed, remove any support structures and ensure smooth movement of the hinges.
4) Attach your chosen bait to the Spomb.
The printable plastic parts are:
1 x KEY
1 x SPOMB 1
1 x SPOMB 2
1 x CIRCLE
Below are the specifications for printing:
FIRST LAYER HEIGHT: 0.2 mm
LAYERS HEIGHT: 0.2 MM
INFILL: 10%
SUPPORT: YES
The non-printable materials required to complete the assembly are:
1 x Ø4 mm SPRING (you can bring it from an old ballpoint pen)
1 x Ø3 mm x 25 mm smooth rod
1 x Ø3 mm x 90 mm smooth rod

I originally made this just because I'd finally managed to wrap my head around making a 3D Printed sphere which would lock together at the equator, and then I tried to think of what I could use it for. Since I'd already made The BeeBar I thought this one would be better for a more sheltered method of topping up our little stripy friends. The butterflies wings are animated with shape keys. A noise modifier on the shape key keyframes makes the wings flap randomly. The butterfly models also have a noise modifier on the Z location, to make the butterflies move randomly up and down.
How to Animate:
There are two methods for animating: Animating the butterflies manually, or animating them along a curve. To animate manually, you can animate the sphere empty object, that the butterflies are parented too. Or to animate along the curve, you can animate the Evaluation Time on the curve data properties, under: Path Animation
Check out the video preview to learn how to use the product.
Contents:  When purchased you will get a zip file containing all of the product files.

  - Animated Butterflies Blender File

  - 5 Butterfly Image Textures

  - HDRI Lighting

Tutorial:
To learn how to make this yourself, and to learn how to use the product, you can watch the tutorial with the video preview.

description_text:
The Moonlit Death Fairy is a captivating 3D creation that merges gothic fantasy with playful, toy-like charm. Designed with a strong Halloween-inspired aesthetic, this character embodies both darkness and beauty in equal measure. With delicate yet eerie moth-like wings, their surfaces shimmer with an iridescent glow of moon dust, creating a mesmerizing play of light that shifts with every angle. Each detail is highly stylized, brought to life with bold, thick lines and deeply etched embossing that make the figure visually striking and tactilely rich.
The fairy’s form captures an ethereal presence—part innocent, part haunting. Its toy-like proportions bring a sense of cuteness and approachability, while its gothic undertones add an air of mystery and intrigue. The shimmering textures across its wings and body suggest a connection to the lunar realm, as though it has been born from moonlight itself, trailing dust of silver and violet hues.
Set against a neutral middle-grey background, the design allows every carved feature and stylized embellishment to stand out with clarity. The craftsmanship is meticulously balanced: smooth, rounded toy-like contours meet with sharp gothic details, from the finely textured patterns on the wings to the subtle embossed motifs adorning its outfit.
This piece functions beautifully as a stylized character model for fantasy, gothic, or Halloween-themed projects, or simply as a collectible digital artwork that blends cuteness with the macabre. The Moonlit Death Fairy is not just a model—it is a narrative piece, carrying with it the imagery of moonlit rituals, enchanted night flights, and the haunting beauty of fairies who dwell in the shadow of the moon.

description_text:
The Celestial Obsidian Scorpion is a striking 3D model that fuses the elegance of cosmic mythology with the menace of nature’s most iconic predator. Forged from the interplay of obsidian and brushed steel, this sculpture-like creation radiates both artistry and danger, making it a perfect centerpiece for stylized renders, fantasy worlds, or collectible design showcases.
The main body is crafted from volcanic obsidian, rendered with subtle roughness that contrasts against areas of smooth polish, catching dramatic light in fractured highlights. Its surface is not plain; instead, etched constellations and glowing silver runes trace across the carapace, suggesting a creature that is both earthly and celestial. The etched details shimmer faintly under the light, creating a mystical aura that blends ancient craftsmanship with astral mystery.
Supporting this volcanic body are segments of brushed steel, modeled with deliberate micro-scratches and slight imperfections to ground the material in realism. The metallic sheen adds sharp definition to the legs and pincers, enhancing the model’s sense of precision and danger. Every curve of the exoskeleton feels both engineered and organic, like a fusion of weapon and creature.
The focal point of the piece lies in the sapphire stinger, a faceted gemstone shard embedded at the tip of the curved tail. Glowing faintly from within, the sapphire refracts light into deep oceanic blues, contrasting vividly against the dark obsidian body. This gemstone detail transforms the scorpion into more than a predator—it becomes a relic, an artifact of power, perhaps even a guardian bound by celestial forces.
Designed for dramatic presentation, the model is fully PBR-textured with high-quality maps: rough obsidian surfaces, brushed steel scratches, and crystalline gemstone shaders that interact beautifully with dynamic lighting. Optimized for performance yet detailed enough for close-up renders, it is suitable for stylized showcases, cinematic storytelling, or fantasy/sci-fi concept art.
The Celestial Obsidian Scorpion balances elegance and menace, making it equally at home in environments such as a mystic artifact chamber, a dark fantasy RPG bestiary, or a futuristic gallery of relics. Its glowing runes and sapphire stinger hint at stories untold, inviting creators to embed it into worlds of myth, science fiction, or cosmic fantasy.

description_text:
The Crystal Arachnid – Glowing Stylized Spider is a unique and striking 3D model designed to bring both mystery and menace into fantasy and sci-fi environments. Forged in the aesthetic of crystalline structures and magical creatures, this spider stands out with its angular geometry, glowing body, and eerie luminescence that makes it feel like a guardian of caverns, dungeons, or alien worlds.
Its design combines organic form with sharp, faceted crystalline edges, giving it a hybrid appearance that feels both natural and otherworldly. The spider’s body is built from interlocking crystal-like plates, each reflecting light with a subtle shimmer. Its eight angular legs are long and jagged, resembling shards of cut gemstones, giving the impression of both fragility and lethal sharpness. The glowing eyes and thorax emit an ethereal light, suggesting magical energy coursing through its form.
Textured with stylized emissive materials, the spider radiates a supernatural glow that works perfectly in dark environments, from glowing caverns to haunted ruins. The emissive effect enhances immersion in fantasy RPGs, dungeon crawlers, or alien landscapes, where this arachnid can serve as a formidable enemy, an ambient creature, or even a mystical guardian of treasures hidden deep underground.
Optimized for game development, the model balances low-poly efficiency with high visual impact, making it ideal for Unity, Unreal Engine, or VR/AR projects. The crystalline surface responds well to different lighting conditions, adding depth and drama to scenes when illuminated by torches, magic spells, or futuristic lighting.
Whether placed as a lurking enemy in a dungeon, a glowing pet in a fantasy village, or an alien insectoid species in a sci-fi setting, the Crystal Arachnid adds intrigue, danger, and wonder. It is more than a creature—it is a visual storytelling piece that sparks curiosity and unease wherever it appears.

description_text:
Step back in time with this masterfully crafted 3D model of a Triceratops, a breathtakingly realistic recreation of one of the most iconic dinosaurs to ever walk the Earth. This model captures the full majesty and scientific accuracy of the three-horned herbivore, from its massive, intricately textured bony frill to the signature trio of horns that define its unmistakable profile. Every detail has been designed to evoke both the power and gentleness of this prehistoric giant its thick, weathered skin bears the marks of age and survival, while intelligent, expressive eyes hint at the complex social behaviors paleontologists believe it once displayed.
The model is posed dynamically, either mid-stride as it patrols its territory or in a defensive stance, ready to protect its kind from predators. Its coloration reflects modern scientific theories earthy greens and browns blend with subtle, vibrant patterns inspired by large herbivores like elephants and rhinos, balancing plausibility with striking visual appeal. The Triceratops fits naturally into lush, late Cretaceous environments, surrounded by ferns, cycads, and primitive flowering plants, all enhanced by dramatic lighting that brings out every scale, scar, and shadow.
This high-resolution model is ideal for cinematic scenes, educational content, scientific visualizations, and museum-quality displays. Designed with clean topology and exquisite surface detail, it offers a living, breathing window into deep time—transforming ancient history into something that feels vividly present and real
